questions.question: Which statement about dynamic programming (DP) as a method for an optimization problem is correct?
options: It takes at each stage the decision with the lowest immediate cost, then moves on
It lists every complete policy and evaluates the total cost of each of them separately
It splits it into related subproblems and computes their optimal values recursively
It solves each stage's subproblem once, independently of the values found at other stages

questions.question: In dynamic programming (DP), a problem is split into stages, and at each stage the process is in one of several states. What is the role of the state?
options: It records the total cost of the cheapest complete policy so far
It records the decision that is taken at this stage of the problem
It records how many stages are left until the end of the horizon
It records the information needed to link this stage to the next

questions.question: A dynamic programming (DP) calculation stores, for every state, its optimal value and also the decision that attains it. Why are the minimizing decisions stored as well?
options: So that an optimal policy can be traced back from the final state
So that the optimal value of the final state can be computed at all
So that only one optimal policy is left when several tie in cost
So that fewer arcs need evaluating in the next stage's recursion

questions.question: Why does dynamic programming (DP) usually need far fewer calculations than enumerating every complete policy of a staged problem?
options: It only follows routes through the cheapest state at each of the stages
Subproblems sharing a state are solved once and their values reused
It stops as soon as one complete policy from start to end has been found
It ignores every stage whose states all have the same optimal value

questions.question: A forward recursion on a staged network with start $S$ and end $T$ computes $f(v)$, the least cost of a route from $S$ to node $v$, as $f(v)=\min_{u\to v}\{c(u,v)+f(u)\}$, where $c(u,v)$ is the cost of arc $u\to v$. Which boundary condition starts it?
options: $f(T)=0$ at the end node $T$
$f(S)=\min_v c(S,v)$ over arcs out of $S$
$f(v)=0$ for each stage-1 node $v$
$f(S)=0$ at the start node $S$

questions.question: A staged network runs from start $S$ to stage-1 nodes $A$, $B$, then stage-2 nodes $C$, $D$, then end $E$. Arc costs: $S\to A$ 4, $S\to B$ 2, $A\to C$ 3, $A\to D$ 6, $B\to C$ 7, $B\to D$ 4, $C\to E$ 5, $D\to E$ 7. If $f(v)$ denotes the least cost of a route from $S$ to node $v$, what is $f(C)$?

Arcs of a staged network from start $S$ (stage 1: $A$, $B$; stage 2: $C$, $D$; end $E$) cost $S\to A$ 4, $S\to B$ 2, $A\to C$ 3, $A\to D$ 6, $B\to C$ 7, $B\to D$ 4, $C\to E$ 5, $D\to E$ 7. What is the least cost of a route from $S$ to $E$?

A forward recursion from start $S$ to end $E$ stored these values and minimizing predecessors: $f(A)=4$ and $f(B)=2$ (both from $S$), $f(C)=7$ from $A$, $f(D)=6$ from $B$, $f(E)=12$ from $C$, where $f(v)$ denotes the least cost of a route from $S$ to node $v$. Which route is optimal?
options: $S\to A\to C\to E$
$S\to B\to D\to E$
$S\to B\to C\to E$
$S\to A\to D\to E$

questions.question: A staged network has a start node, then three stages of 4 nodes each, then an end node, with an arc from every node to every node of the next stage. How many complete start-to-end routes would full enumeration examine?

In a forward recursion on a staged network, node $X$ has three predecessors with stored least costs from the start of 5, 8 and 3, and the arcs from them into $X$ cost 6, 2 and 9 respectively. What is the least cost from the start to $X$?

In a forward recursion on a staged network, two arcs into node $C$ give the same minimal value of arc cost plus predecessor value, and only one of these minimizing predecessors is stored. What is the consequence?
options: One optimal policy can still be traced, but others may be missed
The traced policy may be non-optimal, as one predecessor was lost
The value at $C$ is wrong; it should add the two equal minimal values
The recursion must stop at $C$, as the next stage needs a unique value

questions.question: A forward recursion on a staged network with start $S$ sets $f(S)=0$ and $f(v)=\min_{u\to v}\{c(u,v)+f(u)\}$, where $c(u,v)$ is the cost of arc $u\to v$. What does the computed value $f(C)$ of a stage-2 node $C$ represent?
options: The least cost of any route from $C$ to the end
The least cost of any route from $S$ to $C$
The cost of the cheapest single arc into $C$
The cost of the cheapest-next-arc route to $C$

questions.question: A hiker plans a four-day trek and each night chooses one campsite from a list for that night; the walking cost depends only on the campsites of consecutive nights. In a dynamic programming (DP) model, what are the stages and the states?
options: Stages are the days; states are the next site chosen
Stages are the campsites; states are the days walked
Stages are the days; states are the walking costs
Stages are the days; states are the campsite reached

questions.question: A staged network has a start node, three stages of 4 nodes each and an end node, with an arc from every node to every node of the next stage. A forward recursion evaluates each arc once as arc cost plus predecessor value. How many such evaluations does it make?

Network: start $S$; stage 1 $A$, $B$; stage 2 $C$, $D$; end $E$. Arc costs $S\to A$ 4, $S\to B$ 2, $A\to C$ 3, $A\to D$ 6, $B\to C$ 7, $B\to D$ 4, $C\to E$ 5, $D\to E$ 7. A forward recursion gives least costs 7 to $C$ and 6 to $D$. What is the least cost of a route from $S$ to $E$ that passes through $D$?

A staged network has start $S$, stage-1 nodes $A$, $B$, $C$ with least costs from $S$ of 3, 5 and 4, stage-2 nodes $D$, $E$, and end $T$. Arc costs: $A\to D$ 6, $B\to D$ 2, $C\to D$ 4, $A\to E$ 5, $B\to E$ 4, $C\to E$ 6, $D\to T$ 6, $E\to T$ 4. What is the least cost from $S$ to $T$?

In a network $S\to\{A,B\}\to C\to T$, arcs cost $S\to A$ 1, $S\to B$ 2, $A\to C$ 1, $B\to C$ 1, $C\to T$ 1, but $C\to T$ costs 5 extra on any route that passed through $A$. Which change makes a forward stage-by-stage recursion give the least-cost route?
options: Store every minimizing predecessor at each node, not just one of them
Let the state record both the current node and the stage-1 node used
At each stage, take the cheapest arc leaving the node currently reached
Keep the current node as state but add 5 to the cost of every arc into $T$

questions.question: In a staged network, the route $S\to A\to C\to E$ is a least-cost route from start $S$ to end $E$. What can be concluded about its first part $S\to A\to C$?
options: It is also a least-cost route from $S$ to node $C$
It need not be a least-cost route from $S$ to $C$
It is least-cost only if $A\to C$ is cheapest into $C$
It is least-cost only if $A$ is the cheapest stage-1 node

questions.question: A network has arcs $S\to A$ cost 1, $S\to B$ cost 3, $A\to T$ cost $x$ and $B\to T$ cost 4. The rule 'take the cheapest arc out of the current node' goes $S\to A\to T$. What is the smallest integer $x$ for which this route costs strictly more than the least-cost route?

A staged network has start $S$, stage-1 nodes $A$, $B$, stage-2 nodes $C$, $D$ and end $T$, with arc costs $S\to A$ 2, $S\to B$ 3, $A\to C$ 4, $A\to D$ 5, $B\to C$ 3, $B\to D$ 4, $C\to T$ 3, $D\to T$ 3. How many different least-cost routes from $S$ to $T$ are there?
